title: The Kimchi Notebook
source_body:
The Kimchi Notebook

Every year on the last Saturday of November, Yerin's whole family gathered at her grandmother's house for gimjang, the day of making kimchi for winter.

This year, there were 50 heads of cabbage waiting in the yard. Yerin sighed. "Grandma, why don't we just buy kimchi at the store? It's so much easier."

Her grandmother smiled but didn't answer. She just handed Yerin a pair of rubber gloves.

All morning, they salted cabbage and mixed red pepper powder with garlic, ginger, and fish sauce. By lunchtime, Yerin's back was sore, and she had stopped complaining only because she was too tired to talk.

Then her grandmother began packing the kimchi into boxes. One box was for each of three neighbors who lived alone, and five boxes were for the children's center down the street.

"I have made kimchi like this for 50 years," her grandmother said. "My mother used to do the same. Gimjang is not just about kimchi. It's about sharing."

That night, Yerin opened a new notebook and wrote down every step of her grandmother's recipe. On the first page, she wrote, "Grandma's Kimchi – for sharing."

variants.prestudy:
The Kimchi Notebook

Every year on the final Saturday of November, Yerin's extended family would convene at her grandmother's house for gimjang, the time-honored ritual of preparing kimchi to sustain the household throughout the winter.

This year, no fewer than 50 heads of cabbage lay stacked in the yard, awaiting preparation. Yerin heaved a sigh. "Grandma, why don't we just purchase kimchi at the store? It would be considerably more convenient."

Her grandmother smiled but offered no reply. Instead, she wordlessly handed Yerin a pair of rubber gloves.

Throughout the morning, they salted the cabbage and combined red pepper powder with garlic, ginger, and fish sauce. By lunchtime, Yerin's back was aching, and she had ceased complaining solely because she was too exhausted to utter a word.

Afterward, her grandmother began packing the kimchi into containers. One box was designated for each of the three neighbors who lived by themselves, while five boxes were set aside for the children's center down the street.

"I have prepared kimchi in this manner for half a century," her grandmother explained. "My mother used to do precisely the same. Gimjang has never been merely about kimchi. Fundamentally, it's about sharing."

That night, Yerin opened a brand-new notebook and meticulously documented every step of her grandmother's recipe. On the very first page, she inscribed, "Grandma's Kimchi – for sharing."
